findings.text: The opening paragraph tells a newcomer what Athena is and what sets it apart, in plain words. A first-time reader can say what the tool is after one paragraph.
findings.source: Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository. It shows how it read the request, has one AI model do the work and a different one check it, and records what each step cost.

findings.text: The page says early that it is a demo study of a different project, so the switch from Athena to firstmate makes sense. Still, almost all of the page is about firstmate. Someone who came to learn about Athena gets two sentences about it, and the case for using Athena rests on the reader working out what the study demonstrates.
findings.source: This page is that study of firstmate. Each statement below ends with the id of the claim that supports it

findings.text: The header links straight to the next steps, so a newcomer doesn't have to scroll through the whole state machine to find out what to do.
findings.source: Next step: install Athena or read firstmate itself

findings.text: The install step leaves out the clone command, the prerequisites (a Rust toolchain? AI model API keys?), and what `athena ask` acts on. A newcomer will probably have to go to the repo before they can run anything.
findings.source: Next steps: "Install Athena from a checkout of its repository: ./setup.sh" / "Try it with a one-line request: athena ask "add a changelog""

findings.text: The 'Start here' section works well. It defines words before using them, gives a one-sentence summary of firstmate, walks through one task from start to finish, and lists the failure cases. A newcomer can follow firstmate's basic flow from this section alone.
The page says plainly when its source is silent instead of guessing. This builds trust, but it leaves 'in scope', a key condition for auto-merge, undefined for the reader.
findings.source: in scope: "The cited instruction does not say what makes work in scope, so this page gives no test for it."

findings.text: Some transition cards pack several conditions into one long sentence. A newcomer can't easily scan them, and the dense terms (exit 75, pending-close record, places-held) pile up.
findings.source: t4 Guard: "worktree clean and committed work landed, whether the captain approved the merge, firstmate merged it under yolo, or a local-only ship landed by a guarded fast-forward; a local-only project also counts work merged into the local default branch, and a merge made under yolo may leave no recorded PR (checked by code)"

findings.text: The page states openly that nothing was run and that a first reading missed some paths. A careful reader learns how far to trust the claims.
findings.source: Limits of this study: "This study read the pinned tree only... no failure or retry edge was observed; every claim is marked read."

findings.text: This section refers to a `studies/` folder without saying which repository it is in, so it means nothing to a first-time visitor.
findings.source: About this page: "is the name of the folder under studies/ that holds the data this page is generated from."
